title: Class loading: loaders, delegation, linking and initialization
goal: By the end you can say which loader defines a class and why, predict exactly when a static initializer runs, and read a NoClassDefFoundError or a class that "cannot be cast to" itself for what it really means.

warmup.q: `Limits` has `static final int MAX_MINOR = 500_000;`, `static final Integer CAP = 500_000;` and a `static {}` block that prints "init". Another class prints `Limits.MAX_MINOR`, then `Limits.CAP`. When does "init" appear?
options: Before the first value, because touching any member of a class initializes it
Between the two values: reading `MAX_MINOR` doesn't initialize `Limits`, reading `CAP` does
Never, because both fields are `static final`
Twice, once per field
warmup.why: `MAX_MINOR` is a constant variable: a `static final` primitive with a constant initializer. javac copies `500000` into the caller's class file, so the caller never touches `Limits` at run time. `CAP` is boxed (`Integer.valueOf` runs), so it is not a constant, and reading it runs `Limits`'s static initializer. A class initializes at most once, so "init" can't print twice.

sections.h: Every class has a defining loader, and it is part of the class's identity
sections.body:
Ask three classes who loaded them and you get three different answers:

```java
System.out.println(String.class.getClassLoader());              // null
System.out.println(java.sql.Connection.class.getClassLoader());  // ...ClassLoaders$PlatformClassLoader@<hash>
System.out.println(PaymentApp.class.getClassLoader());          // ...ClassLoaders$AppClassLoader@<hash>
```

```kotlin
println(String::class.java.classLoader)                // null
println(java.sql.Connection::class.java.classLoader)   // ...ClassLoaders$PlatformClassLoader@<hash>
println(PaymentApp::class.java.classLoader)            // ...ClassLoaders$AppClassLoader@<hash>
```

The JDK has three built-in class loaders. The bootstrap loader is part of the JVM and loads `java.base`; the `ClassLoader` Javadoc says it is "typically represented as `null`". The platform loader loads the other Java SE and JDK modules, such as `java.sql` and `java.net.http`. The app loader (also called the system loader) loads your class path: your code, Quarkus, the Kafka client, the Kotlin standard library. Each one has the next as its parent: app, then platform, then bootstrap. JDK 21 and JDK 25 print the same chain.

When code asks a loader for a class, the default `loadClass` does three things in order. It checks whether this loader already has the name (`findLoadedClass`). If not, it asks its parent, which asks its own parent first. Only when every parent fails does it call its own `findClass`. So `java.lang.String` always comes from the bootstrap loader, even if some jar on your class path contains a class with that name. This is **parent-first delegation**. It's why a stray jar can't replace a JDK class.

The loader that finally calls `defineClass` is the class's defining loader, and it is part of the class's identity. At run time a class is the pair (binary name, defining loader). Two loaders that each define `com.acme.Money` from the same bytes produce two classes that happen to share a name. You'll build exactly that in the lab, and section 4 shows what it does to a cast.

Kotlin adds nothing special here. `kotlin.Unit` is an ordinary class in an ordinary jar, so the app loader defines it like any other library class.

sections.h: Loading, linking and initialization are three steps, and only the last runs your code
sections.body:
Loading a class and running its `static {}` block are separate events. Chapter 5 of the JVM specification splits the work into three phases, and HotSpot runs each one as late as it is allowed to.

1. Loading finds the bytes (in a jar, a directory, or generated in memory) and turns them into a `Class` object with `defineClass`.
2. Linking checks and prepares the class. Verification proves the bytecode is type-safe. Preparation creates the static fields and sets them to their defaults: `0`, `false`, `null`. Resolution turns symbolic references in the constant pool ("method `charge` in class `Ledger`") into direct ones, and may do it lazily, one reference at a time.
3. Initialization runs the class's static initializer, which javac names `<clinit>`: every static field initializer and `static {}` block, in source order.

Two small experiments show the gaps between the phases. A generated class with broken bytecode was accepted by `ClassLoader.defineClass` on JDK 25, and the `VerifyError` appeared only when code first asked for its methods. A class that referenced a deleted `Helper` class loaded and ran fine. It failed with `NoClassDefFoundError` only when the branch that used `Helper` executed.

Initialization is the phase your code can see, and its triggers are precise. JLS section 12.4.1 lists them: creating an instance, calling a static method, assigning a static field, or reading a static field that is not a **constant variable**. Initializing a class first initializes its superclass. Reflection such as `Class.forName(name)` or a reflective static field read counts too.

These do not initialize a class:

- reading a `static final` primitive or `String` that has a constant initializer, because javac copied the value into your class file;
- `Limits.class`, `new Limits[3]` and `Class.forName(name, false, loader)`;
- reading an inherited static field through a subclass name: `Child.parentValue` initializes only `Parent`, the class that declares the field.

The constant rule surprises people most. `static final int MAX_MINOR = 500_000` is a constant variable. `static final Integer CAP = 500_000` is not, because boxing calls `Integer.valueOf`. Reading the first leaves `Limits` alone. Reading the second runs `<clinit>`. Kotlin draws the same line between `const val` and a plain `val`.

Predict the three `hits` values and whether the cast at the end works.
Run it (or the Kotlin twin) and find the two loader names in the exception message.

code.title: TwoLoadersDemo.java

alt.title: TwoLoadersDemo.kt

try.expect: `same name: true`, `c1 == c2: false` and `c1 == Counter.class: false`. The hits are `plugin-1=2, plugin-2=0, app=0`: three classes, three separate static fields. The cast fails with `... cannot be cast to class ...$Counter`, and the parentheses name loader `'plugin-1'` and loader `'app'`.

analogy: A class name is like an account number, and the defining loader is the bank. Account 4471 at two banks is two accounts with two balances, and a transfer form for one bank rejects the other bank's account even though the numbers match. Parent-first delegation is a branch that always asks head office whether it already holds the account before it opens a new one, so nobody can open a second "java.lang.String". The analogy breaks in one place: two copies of a class are not strangers. They come from the same bytes and share everything their parent loaded, such as `String` and the interfaces they implement, which is why a plugin can still be used through a shared interface.
in_your_world: Picture an FX service that loads its rate table in a static initializer: `static final RateTable RATES = RateTable.load(Path.of("rates.csv"))`. In a Quarkus test run the file isn't on the test path. The first test fails with `ExceptionInInitializerError`, and the next forty fail with `NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class RateTable`, which sends people looking for a missing dependency. The same class under Quarkus dev mode is defined again by a fresh Runtime ClassLoader on every reload, so a static cache in a parent-first library that keeps old `RateTable` objects pins the old classes in memory. Load data in a bean that the container starts, and keep statics to constants.
mistake: The common mistake is reading `NoClassDefFoundError` as "a jar is missing" and adding dependencies until it goes away. Often the jar is fine: the class's static initializer threw once, earlier, and the JVM now refuses that class for the life of its loader. People make this mistake because the later error is the one that fills the log, and its name sounds like a class-path problem. The fix is to search the log for the first `ExceptionInInitializerError` (or read the cause of the `NoClassDefFoundError` on JDK 21 and later), fix what threw, and move I/O and configuration out of static initializers into lazy or container-managed code.

compare.title: When static initialization runs, in Java and Kotlin

java.title: Limits.java

kotlin.title: Limits.kt

compare.note: Kotlin has no `static`, but an `object` compiles to a class with a `public static final INSTANCE` field and a static initializer that builds it, so the JVM rules are the same. Only `const val` (primitives and `String`) is inlined into callers like a Java constant variable. A plain `val` in an object becomes a private static field plus a getter, so reading it touches the class and runs its `init` blocks. Companion objects follow the same rules, and their `init` code lands in the outer class's `static {}` block, which is why the Kotlin `FeeSchedule` in section 3 reads 0 exactly like the Java one.

worked.title: Read a NoClassDefFoundError back to its cause

steps.say: A Quarkus test run shows this, forty times. Before reading on, decide: is a jar missing?
steps.code:
java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class com.acme.fx.RateTable
    at com.acme.fx.QuoteService.quote(QuoteService.java:31)
    ...
Caused by: java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError: Exception java.lang.IllegalStateException:
    rates file missing: rates.csv [in thread "executor-thread-1"]

steps.say: No. "Could not initialize class" means the JVM found `RateTable` and already tried to initialize it. The cause (JDK 21 and later) points at the first failure. Here is the class. Each chunk of `<clinit>` runs once, in order.

Move the I/O out of class initialization. A bean the container builds at startup fails once, with a clear stack trace, and a fixed file or a restart of the test fixes it. The class itself has no static state left to poison.

If the value must stay static, make it lazy with a holder class (memory model track, lesson 5). A failure still poisons the holder, but only callers that need the table see it, and the error appears at the first real use instead of whenever some unrelated class touched `RateTable`.

lab.title: Fix an initialization-order bug, then load one class twice
steps: Run the tests once. Eight of ten fail: the unknown-country fee comes back as 0, and every loader test hits `UnsupportedOperationException`.

In `FeeSchedule`, read the static fields from top to bottom as `<clinit>` runs them. Move one line so the constructor sees the real `DEFAULT_BPS`. Don't change any number. Ask yourself why `currency()` was right all along.

In `IsolatingLoader.findClass`, read the class file through the parent with `getParent().getResourceAsStream(name.replace('.', '/') + ".class")`, then call `defineClass(name, bytes, 0, bytes.length)`. Throw `ClassNotFoundException` when the stream is null.

In `loadClass`, take `getClassLoadingLock(name)`. Return `findLoadedClass(name)` if it isn't null. For names that start with the prefix, call `findClass`. For everything else, return `super.loadClass(name, resolve)`.
Run the tests until all ten pass. Then read `castAcrossLoadersFails` and find which loader names appear in the message.
hints: Constants such as `"EUR"` are inlined by javac, so their order doesn't matter. `Integer.parseInt(...)` is a method call, so `DEFAULT_BPS` is 0 until `<clinit>` reaches its line.
If a test fails with `LinkageError: attempted duplicate class definition`, your `loadClass` defined the same name twice. Check `findLoadedClass` first.
Don't call `super.loadClass` for prefix names before `findClass`: the parent would find the app's copy and you'd get the same `Class` from both loaders.

drill.title: A child-first loader from memory
drill.prompt: Close this page and the lab. Write `loadClass(String name, boolean resolve)` for a loader that defines classes under `prefix` itself and delegates everything else to its parent. Then check: did you take the class-loading lock, and did you look for an already-loaded class before defining one?

recap: Three built-in loaders: bootstrap (`null`, `java.base`), platform (other JDK modules), app (your class path). They delegate parent-first.
A class is (binary name, defining loader). The same bytes defined by two loaders are two classes with separate statics, and casts between them fail.
Loading, linking (verify, prepare, resolve) and initialization are separate and lazy. Only initialization runs `<clinit>`.
Initialization triggers: `new`, a static call, a non-constant static read or write, reflection, a subclass. Constants, `X.class`, arrays and `forName(n, false, l)` don't trigger it.

`<clinit>` runs once, in source order, under a lock. A throw gives `ExceptionInInitializerError` once, then `NoClassDefFoundError` forever. Two initializers that need each other can deadlock with both threads RUNNABLE.
`ClassNotFoundException` is an explicit lookup failing. `NoClassDefFoundError` is the JVM failing to link or initialize a class your code was compiled against.

quiz.q: `class Parent { static int rate = 290; static { log("Parent"); } }` and `class Child extends Parent { static { log("Child"); } }`. Fresh JVM: your code reads `Child.rate`. What is logged?
options: `Parent` then `Child`
Only `Child`
Only `Parent`
Nothing, because `rate` is static
quiz.why: A static field reference initializes only the class that declares the field, even when you name it through a subclass. `rate` is declared in `Parent`, so only `Parent` runs. `Parent` then `Child` is what `new Child()` or a static method declared in `Child` would log.

quiz.q: A service's logs show `NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class com.acme.BinTable` on every request since startup. What do you look for first?
options: A `bin-table` jar missing from the image
An earlier `ExceptionInInitializerError` (or the NCDFE's cause) showing what `BinTable`'s static initializer threw
A second copy of `BinTable` in another jar
A JIT deoptimization of `BinTable`
quiz.why: "Could not initialize class" means the JVM found the class and its initializer already failed once; the class stays failed for the life of its loader. The first failure was an `ExceptionInInitializerError`, and on JDK 21 the NCDFE's cause names it. A missing jar shows up as an NCDFE caused by `ClassNotFoundException` instead.

quiz.q: A Quarkus test fails with `class com.acme.Money cannot be cast to class com.acme.Money (com.acme.Money is in unnamed module of loader 'Quarkus Runtime ClassLoader' ...; com.acme.Money is in unnamed module of loader 'app')`. What happened?
options: Two different versions of `Money` were compiled
The JVM's class cache is corrupt
`Money` was defined by two loaders, and an object from one copy met a variable typed with the other
`Money` is missing a no-argument constructor
quiz.why: The same name with two different loaders is two different classes, even from identical bytes. The fix is to make sure both sides use the same copy, for example by not holding `Money` objects in something the app loader owns, or by adjusting what is loaded parent-first. Recompiling changes nothing, because the bytes were never the problem.

quiz.q: At startup two threads hang. Both are `RUNNABLE` with a top frame in a `<clinit>`, and `findDeadlockedThreads()` returns null. What is the most likely cause?
options: A class-initialization deadlock: two static initializers that need each other, started from two threads
A busy loop, because the threads are RUNNABLE
Lock contention on a `synchronized` method
A full GC pause
quiz.why: Threads waiting for another thread's class initialization show as RUNNABLE, and the JDK's deadlock detector doesn't report them. `jstack` gives it away with `waiting on the Class initialization monitor for ...`. Break the cycle so one initializer no longer reads the other class's statics.

quiz.q: From *Lazy init done right*: the holder idiom puts `static final CardBinTable INSTANCE = new CardBinTable();` in a nested `Holder` class. Why doesn't the table get built when the outer class `CardBinTable` is initialized?
options: Nested classes are loaded by a different class loader
`Holder` is a separate class, and nothing initializes it until `instance()` reads `Holder.INSTANCE`
The JIT removes unused static fields
`static final` fields are always initialized lazily
quiz.why: A nested class is its own class with its own `<clinit>`. Initializing the outer class doesn't touch it. The first read of `Holder.INSTANCE` is a non-constant static read, which triggers `Holder`'s initialization once, under the JVM's class-init lock. That lock is also why the idiom is thread-safe without `volatile`.

flashcards.front: Which loader defines `java.lang.String`, and how does `getClassLoader()` show it?
flashcards.back: The bootstrap loader, built into the JVM. `String.class.getClassLoader()` returns `null`.

flashcards.front: In what order does the default `loadClass` look for a class?
flashcards.back: `findLoadedClass` (already defined here?), then the parent's `loadClass`, then its own `findClass`.

flashcards.front: Does reading `static final int MAX = 500;` from another class initialize the declaring class?
flashcards.back: No. It's a constant variable, so javac copied 500 into the caller. `static final Integer MAX = 500;` is not a constant and does initialize it.

flashcards.front: Your code reads `Child.x`, where static field `x` is declared in `Parent`. Which classes initialize?
flashcards.back: Only `Parent`, the class that declares the field.

flashcards.front: A static initializer throws. What do the first and the later uses of the class get?
flashcards.back: First use: `ExceptionInInitializerError`. Every later use: `NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class ...`. The JVM never retries.

flashcards.front: How does a class-initialization deadlock look in a thread dump?
flashcards.back: Threads in `RUNNABLE` state, `waiting on the Class initialization monitor for ...`, and no "Found one Java-level deadlock" section.

flashcards.front: Two loaders define `com.acme.Money` from the same bytes. Is `b.isInstance(objectFromA)` true?
flashcards.back: No. A class is (name, defining loader), so these are two classes. A cast between them throws ClassCastException naming both loaders.

terms.plain: An object that finds class bytes and turns them into `Class` objects. The JDK has bootstrap, platform and app loaders.
A loader asks its parent for a class before trying to find it itself.
The loader that called `defineClass`. It is part of the class's identity.
Verifying, preparing (static fields set to defaults) and resolving a loaded class, before it is initialized.
The static initializer javac builds from static field initializers and `static {}` blocks, run once per class.
A `final` primitive or `String` with a compile-time constant initializer. javac copies its value into the code that reads it.
A custom loader that defines certain classes itself before asking its parent, to isolate plugins or reloadable code.

explain_back.prompt: A teammate sees `NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class FeeSchedule` in production and wants to add `fees-core.jar` to the image. Explain what the error really says, how you'd find the cause, and how to stop it happening again.
explain_back.answer: The JVM found `FeeSchedule` fine. It already tried to run its static initializer once, that initializer threw, and the JVM marked the class as failed, so every later use gets `NoClassDefFoundError` and it never retries. Adding a jar won't help. I'd look for the first `ExceptionInInitializerError` in the log, or read the cause chain, which on JDK 21 names the original exception and thread. The fix is whatever made the initializer throw, plus moving that work out of `<clinit>`: keep statics to constants and do I/O or configuration in a bean the container starts or in a lazy holder, so a failure is an ordinary exception at the call that needs it.

deeper.body:
Three details that didn't fit above.

Interfaces have their own initialization rule. Initializing a class initializes its superclass, but its superinterfaces only if they declare a default method. In one experiment, `new Impl()` for a class implementing `WithDefault` (which has a default method) and `NoDefault` (which doesn't) printed `WithDefault.<clinit>` and `Impl.<clinit>`, and `NoDefault` stayed uninitialized until code read one of its fields. HotSpot's `InstanceKlass::initialize_impl` follows the JVMS steps one by one, and its comments quote this rule.

Lambdas are hidden classes. A lambda's class has a name like `LoaderInfo$$Lambda/0x00007f2408000a08`, `isHidden()` returns true, and `Class.forName` on that name throws `ClassNotFoundException`. `LambdaMetafactory` defines it with `Lookup.defineHiddenClass` (JDK 15) as a nestmate of the class that contains the lambda. Lesson 3 of this track shows the call site that creates it.

You can watch the phases. `-Xlog:class+load=info` prints a line per loaded class with its source, and `-Xlog:class+init=info` prints verification start and end and an `Initializing '...'` line per class. A Hello World with one lambda loaded 560 classes on JDK 21 and 645 on JDK 25, most of them from the CDS archive (`source: shared objects file`). The startup track covers that archive and the AOT cache that JDK 24 and 25 build on it.

```bash
java -Xlog:class+load=info -Xlog:class+init=info -cp bytecode/build/classes/java/demo workbench.bytecode.l01.InitPuzzle | grep -E 'InitPuzzle|Initializing'
```
